 Leon Neal/Getty Images 
 The world is currently being swept up by the latest Grand Theft Auto video game, but could the record-setting franchise one day be a TV series or movie? The answer, according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick: Maybe, in the right circumstances.

 Prior to Grand Theft Auto VI breaking pre-sales records ahead of its official global release tomorrow, Zelnick was asked about “line extensions” for the gaming franchise during a recent appearance on The David Rubenstein Show podcast – to which he gave a measured response.
 “We’re very careful about line extensions because this is a creative company and our goal is to make the best entertainment on earth – entertainment we’re always proud of,” said Zelnick.
 “We would make a movie or television show based on our intellectual property if our creative teams were passionate about it – if they thought they would somehow engage and delight our consumers. It’s a high bar to do that, and of course, there’s always a risk of failure. So we don’t rule it out, but we’re very, very selective.”
 Watch on Deadline 
 Jack Black has previously voiced a desire to appear in a Grand Theft Auto title or another Rockstar game, though Dan Houser, a key player in the franchise’s development, has previously warned a movie was unlikely to ever be made.
 Top-selling video games have become solid bases for TV and film adaptations, with Netflix taking The Witcher to multiple seasons, HBO gaining critical acclaim for its version of The Last of Us and the likes of Super Mario Bros , Sonic the Hedgehog and Minecraft all having successful movies released in recent years. Elden Rings was recently being shopped at the American Film Market.
 Grand Theft Auto , however, has never been adapted, perhaps due to its sprawling and wild nature and each game introducing new protagonists and cities.
 Grand Theft Auto VI , which is the most expensive game ever developed, has taken an estimated $1.5B in pre-sales – far higher than any TV or film series in history and almost double the $800M Grand Theft Auto V bagged in 2013. Reviews have been universally superb, with its current Metacritic score placing it all-time joint first with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time .
 The sandbox game lets the player take control of two characters, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, a Bonnie and Clyde -style couple in Leonida, an open world setting based on Florida. As the eighth main game in the franchise, its development took far longer than any of its predecessors, with a full 13 years between its launch and Grand Theft Auto 5 .
